dataset_name: SIH 26140 Detailed Online Learning Curriculum Dataset
note: Detailed instructional content organized from the official problem statement. The exact chapter structure is a practical curriculum design; the source requirements and named deliverables are preserved.

chapters.title: Introduction to Quantum Computing
chapters.overview: Learn what quantum computing is, how it differs from classical computing, and why concepts such as qubits, superposition and entanglement need interactive learning.
learning_objectives: Understand the purpose of quantum computing.
Know the difference between a classical bit and a qubit.
Recognize the core terms used throughout the platform.

sections.title: What is Quantum Computing?
sections.explanation: Quantum computing is a way of processing information using quantum systems. This course introduces the ideas needed to understand quantum circuits and algorithms through simple explanations and interactive examples.

sections.title: Classical vs Quantum Computing
sections.explanation: Classical computers use bits with values 0 or 1. Quantum computing uses qubits and quantum operations, allowing different ways of representing and manipulating information.

sections.title: Why Learn Quantum Computing Interactively?
sections.explanation: Quantum concepts can be abstract when learned only from text. An interactive platform lets learners build circuits, execute simulations and immediately inspect visual results.

sections.title: Quantum Computing Vocabulary
sections.explanation: Build a basic vocabulary before working in the lab.

key_takeaways: Understand the purpose of quantum computing.
Know the difference between a classical bit and a qubit.
Recognize the core terms used throughout the platform.

chapters.title: Qubits and Quantum States
chapters.overview: Understand the qubit, computational basis states, state representation and the basic idea of a statevector.
learning_objectives: Understand the purpose of a statevector display.
Connect circuit operations with changes in quantum state.

sections.title: What is a Qubit?
sections.explanation: A qubit is the basic unit used to represent quantum information. It can be prepared, transformed with quantum gates and measured.

sections.title: Computational Basis States
sections.explanation: The two standard computational basis states for one qubit are written as |0> and |1>.

sections.title: Quantum State Representation
sections.explanation: A quantum state can be represented mathematically and displayed by a simulator. For the learning platform, learners should be able to inspect the state produced by a circuit.

sections.title: State Changes
sections.explanation: Gates change the state of a qubit. Learners can compare the state before and after applying a gate.

sections.title: Interactive State Explorer
sections.explanation: Use the circuit lab to prepare a state, apply a gate and inspect the resulting state information.

key_takeaways: Understand the purpose of a statevector display.
Connect circuit operations with changes in quantum state.

chapters.title: Superposition and Measurement
chapters.overview: Learn superposition using simple circuits and understand how measurement and repeated shots produce observable outcome distributions.
learning_objectives: Explain the introductory idea of superposition.
Understand why repeated shots are useful.

sections.title: Concept of Superposition
sections.explanation: Superposition is a fundamental quantum concept. The platform introduces it through a visual circuit and simulation rather than only mathematical notation.

sections.title: Hadamard Gate
sections.explanation: The Hadamard gate is a standard example for demonstrating an equal superposition from a computational basis input such as |0>.

sections.title: Measurement
sections.explanation: Measurement produces a classical outcome from a quantum state.

sections.title: Shots and Probability
sections.explanation: Running a circuit repeatedly produces counts that can be converted into empirical probabilities.

sections.title: Measurement Histogram
sections.explanation: A histogram provides a visual view of measurement outcomes and their frequencies/probabilities.

sections.title: Understanding Results
sections.explanation: Compare the expected behavior of a simple circuit with the simulated measurement distribution.

key_takeaways: Explain the introductory idea of superposition.
Understand why repeated shots are useful.

chapters.title: Quantum Gates and Circuits
chapters.overview: Learn common quantum gates and how gates are arranged into single- and multi-qubit circuits.

sections.title: Quantum Gates
sections.explanation: Quantum gates are operations applied to qubits. They form the basic building blocks of a quantum circuit.

sections.title: H Gate
sections.explanation: Use H to explore superposition behavior in the lab.

sections.title: X, Y and Z Gates
sections.explanation: Explore common single-qubit gates and compare their effects.

sections.title: S and T Gates
sections.explanation: Introduce S and T as additional single-qubit gates and show their role in circuit construction.

sections.title: CNOT Gate
sections.explanation: CNOT is a controlled two-qubit operation. One qubit acts as control and another as target.

sections.title: SWAP Gate
sections.explanation: SWAP exchanges the states of two qubits.

sections.title: Circuit Diagram
sections.explanation: Read qubit wires, gate positions and operation order from a circuit diagram.

sections.title: Multi-Qubit Circuits
sections.explanation: Combine multiple gates and qubits into a complete circuit.

chapters.title: Entanglement
chapters.overview: Learn the introductory concept of entanglement and construct a simple Bell-state circuit.
learning_objectives: Explain entanglement at an introductory level.

sections.title: What is Entanglement?
sections.explanation: Entanglement describes quantum correlations between quantum systems. It is introduced through small circuits and measurable outcomes.

sections.title: Bell State
sections.explanation: A Bell-state circuit is a standard learning example that can be built with a Hadamard gate followed by a CNOT.

sections.title: Building the Circuit
sections.explanation: Construct the circuit step by step in the visual editor.

sections.title: Correlated Results
sections.explanation: Inspect the measurement results and understand the correlation shown by the simple Bell-state example.

sections.title: Entanglement Lab Exercise
sections.explanation: Learners build the circuit themselves, run it and explain the result.

key_takeaways: Explain entanglement at an introductory level.

chapters.title: Quantum Circuit Design and Programming
chapters.overview: Learn how to construct circuits visually and with code, validate them and execute them in the quantum lab.
learning_objectives: Validate a circuit before running it.

sections.title: Drag-and-Drop Circuit Builder
sections.explanation: Use a gate palette and place operations on qubit wires.

sections.title: Circuit Editing
sections.explanation: Modify circuits before execution.

sections.title: Multi-Qubit Gate Placement
sections.explanation: Learn how controlled and two-qubit gates occupy multiple qubit wires.

sections.title: Code-Based Circuit Creation
sections.explanation: Create a quantum circuit using supported quantum Python code.

sections.title: Code Editor
sections.explanation: Use a code editor with readable formatting and syntax highlighting.

sections.title: Circuit Validation
sections.explanation: Check for invalid operations before simulation.

sections.title: Visual and Code Views
sections.explanation: Understand that the same circuit can be represented graphically and programmatically.

key_takeaways: Validate a circuit before running it.

chapters.title: Quantum Simulation and Frameworks
chapters.overview: Understand how software simulators execute quantum circuits and how the platform can expose multiple frameworks/backends.

sections.title: What is Quantum Simulation?
sections.explanation: A simulator runs a software model of a quantum circuit so learners can experiment without requiring direct access to physical quantum hardware.

sections.title: Qiskit Aer
sections.explanation: Introduce Qiskit Aer as a simulation backend named in the SIH problem statement.

sections.title: PennyLane
sections.explanation: Introduce PennyLane as another framework named in the SIH problem statement and explain its role as an execution/simulation framework.

sections.title: Cirq
sections.explanation: Introduce Cirq as another named quantum framework.

sections.title: Qbraid
sections.explanation: Introduce Qbraid as a named platform/integration in the problem statement.

sections.title: Backend Selection
sections.explanation: Allow learners to select an available backend and execute the same learning circuit where supported.

sections.title: Shots and Results
sections.explanation: Understand shots, counts, probabilities and basic execution metadata.

chapters.title: Quantum Algorithms
chapters.overview: Explore the standard algorithms explicitly named in the problem statement through structured explanations, circuit examples and simulation.
learning_objectives: Run and inspect small educational examples.

sections.title: What is a Quantum Algorithm?
sections.explanation: A quantum algorithm is a sequence of quantum operations designed to solve or study a computational problem using a quantum system.

sections.title: Deutsch-Jozsa Algorithm
sections.explanation: Study the purpose and circuit structure of Deutsch-Jozsa through a small educational example.

sections.title: Grover's Algorithm
sections.explanation: Study Grover as a quantum search example using a small circuit suitable for interactive simulation.

sections.title: QAOA
sections.explanation: Study QAOA as a parameterized algorithm named in the problem statement.

sections.title: VQE
sections.explanation: Study VQE as a parameterized algorithm named in the problem statement.

sections.title: Algorithm Comparison
sections.explanation: Compare the purpose and interaction pattern of the listed algorithms.

key_takeaways: Run and inspect small educational examples.

chapters.title: Quantum State and Result Visualization
chapters.overview: Learn to interpret the visual outputs required by the platform: circuit rendering, measurement histograms, statevectors and Bloch sphere views.
learning_objectives: Use the Bloch sphere as an interactive learning visualization.

sections.title: Circuit Rendering
sections.explanation: See the circuit as a readable visual sequence of gates and measurements.

sections.title: Measurement Histogram
sections.explanation: Use a histogram to inspect measurement counts or probabilities.

sections.title: Probability Distribution
sections.explanation: Convert measurement counts into an intuitive probability view.

sections.title: Statevector Display
sections.explanation: Inspect amplitudes/state information returned by a simulator where supported.

sections.title: Bloch Sphere
sections.explanation: Use a Bloch sphere visualization to explore a single-qubit state.

sections.title: Reading Visual Results
sections.explanation: Connect visual outputs with the circuit that produced them.

sections.title: Interactive Visualization Exercise
sections.explanation: Change a gate, rerun the circuit and compare the visualization.

key_takeaways: Use the Bloch sphere as an interactive learning visualization.

chapters.title: Assessment, Challenges and Learning Progress
chapters.overview: Check learning through quizzes and practical challenges, calculate performance and track learner progress.

sections.title: Learning Assessment
sections.explanation: Use assessments to verify understanding after lessons.

sections.title: MCQ Quizzes
sections.explanation: Answer structured multiple-choice questions covering course topics.

sections.title: Coding Challenges
sections.explanation: Write quantum code for a specified circuit or task.

sections.title: Circuit Challenges
sections.explanation: Construct a target circuit using the visual circuit designer.

sections.title: Automated Grading
sections.explanation: Evaluate submissions using defined deterministic rules.

sections.title: Progress Tracking
sections.explanation: Store completed lessons, quiz scores and challenge results.

sections.title: Performance Analytics
sections.explanation: Summarize learning performance for the student.

sections.title: Instructor Dashboard
sections.explanation: Provide an instructor view of learner progress and performance as required by the problem statement.

sections.title: Authentication and Web Application
sections.explanation: Provide user authentication and a responsive web application around the learning experience.
